extracted.intended_audience: humor researchers, cognitive psychologists, comedy writers and students of humor theory
extracted.subtask_description: Apply Suls's two-stage information-processing model to analyze or construct jokes: detect an initial prediction/incongruity and provide a discoverable cognitive rule that resolves it to produce humor. Useful for evaluating joke success and pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 — Incongruity Detection
rubrics_metrics.description: The audience processes the setup linearly, generating a prediction about what comes next; the punchline disconfirms that prediction so the audience perceives an incongruity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the setup licenses a definite default prediction and whether the punchline conflicts with that prediction. Anti-pattern: vague setups that fail to license any clear prediction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 — Resolution (Cognitive Rule Discovery)
rubrics_metrics.description: The audience searches for a cognitive rule that makes the punchline make sense in light of the setup by re-examining the setup and finding an alternate interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a plausible reinterpretation exists that subsumes the punchline and whether the audience can find it within available processing time. If the rule is found → humor; if not → puzzlement/nonsense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor requires incongruity followed by resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor results from incongruity that is then resolved, not from incongruity per se.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate mere weirdness or surprise with humor. The key diagnostic: is there a resolvable alternate cognitive frame that retroactively makes the punchline coherent?

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup creates a definite default prediction
rubrics_metrics.description: The setup must license a clear expectation or prediction about the continuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the setup is too vague to license a prediction, the punchline cannot violate one. When constructing or evaluating a setup, state the prediction explicitly to test this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punchline is incongruous with the prediction
rubrics_metrics.description: The punchline must disconfirm the default prediction (i.e., produce surprise/incongruity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A predictable punchline has no surprise and therefore fails this criterion. Check genuineness of incongruity — superficial oddness that doesn't contradict the prediction is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: A discoverable cognitive rule must exist
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be a cognitive rule that subsumes the punchline and makes it compatible with the setup upon reinterpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule must be (a) accessible — audience can find it within processing time, (b) plausible — audience accepts the retrospective fit, and (c) neither trivial nor obscure. Use accessibility and plausibility checks when evaluating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule difficulty must be in the 'sweet spot'
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolution should require some cognitive effort but be achievable within seconds; neither trivial (too easy) nor overly effortful (too hard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical guidance: jokes rate funniest when resolution requires modest effort. Anti-patterns: immediate obvious resolutions (boring) or resolutions that demand lengthy deliberation (puzzling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience processing speed must match joke pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: The audience's processing speed must align with the joke's temporal pacing so incongruity is noticed and resolution can occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If processing is too fast the incongruity may be missed; if too slow tension may dissipate. Consider listener/readers' fluency and time constraints when designing pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward vs. backward resolution (variant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolution may be forward (rule found in the punchline itself) or backward (rule found by re-examining the setup); most jokes use backward resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing jokes, decide whether the punchline should itself supply the rule or primarily trigger reinterpretation of the setup. Use backward resolution to create the satisfying 'aha' reframe for the setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion — Pure incongruity without resolvability
rubrics_metrics.description: Pure incongruity that cannot be resolved leads to bewilderment or surrealism, not the comic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label as anti-pattern: unresolved weirdness. Such material may belong to surrealist art but does not satisfy the model's criteria for producing humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion — Pure congruity (predictable punchline)
rubrics_metrics.description: A purely congruent, predictable punchline produces no humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid punchlines that merely confirm expectations; humor requires violation of the predicted continuation followed by resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion — Resolution that is morally or factually wrong
rubrics_metrics.description: If the discovered resolution is morally or factually wrong, the audience may experience confusion and reject the resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the reinterpretation depends on implausible or unacceptable premises; if so, it will likely produce confusion rather than pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic evaluation questions
rubrics_metrics.description: A checklist of questions to determine whether the model's conditions are met for a given joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these questions to evaluate jokes: What prediction does the setup license? Is the punchline genuinely incongruous with that prediction? What is the resolving cognitive rule and can the audience reasonably find it? Is the resolution at the sweet spot of effort — discoverable but not trivial?

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution outcome — humor vs puzzlement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the resolving cognitive rule is found the audience experiences humor; if no rule is found, the result is puzzlement or the perception of nonsense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing a joke's likely reception, predict the audience's ability to find the rule; inability implies the joke will be perceived as nonsensical rather than funny.
